overview: White sets up the Colle-Zukertort system against ...c5 and ...d5, with pawns on d4, e3 and b3, bishops on d3 and b2, a knight on f3 and another coming to bd2, and castling kingside. Black usually plays 5...Nc6 6.O-O Bd6 7.Bb2 O-O. White's plan is the central break e4 (after Nbd2 and Ne5), a possible kingside attack on h7, or pressure from the b2 bishop on the long diagonal. Black has easy equality and counters with ...cxd4 and ...e5.

white_ideas.idea: Bb2, Nbd2 or Nc3 and Ne5 to prepare the e4 break
Use the b2 bishop and Bd3 for a kingside attack on h7
Keep a solid centre with e3 and d4 and avoid early tactics

black_ideas.idea: Develop ...Nc6, ...Bd6, ...O-O and hit the centre with ...cxd4 or ...e5
Prevent the e4 break by keeping the d5 pawn and covering e4
Trade a pair of minor pieces and aim for equality

typical_structures.structure: White d4/e3/b3 against Black c5/d5/e6 (Colle-Zukertort / hanging-pawn style tension)

character.notes: A classic quiet system with few ways to go wrong quickly; the e4 break is the one sharp moment. Solid.

structure.notes: Centre in tension, e4 break pending; like the London and Colle, this is Flexible.

approach.notes: White reaches the same set-up against almost any Black defence. System.

level.notes: Clear plans and little theory; the kind of line a coach hands a new player. Beginner.

sublines_that_differ.name: 5...Nc6 6.O-O
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. Nf3 Nf6 3. e3 e6 4. Bd3 c5 5. b3 Nc6
sublines_that_differ.how: The main line, where Black develops quickly and White castles and plays Bb2.

character.reason: A quiet system with few risks, though the e4 break can produce attacking chances.

structure.reason: The centre stays in tension and the e4 break decides the structure.

approach.reason: A Colle-Zukertort set-up playable against almost anything.

level.reason: Clear plans and little to memorise, like the Colle and London.

plans.reason: Bb2 on the long diagonal and the e4 break feeding a kingside attack.
